summary: A 1940s six-by-six-foot cabin on Three Creek Butte near Sisters, abandoned and burned in 2002; no source describes the site today.

staffing.status: manned in high-risk weather (1967 annual report)

facts.status_note: Abandoned for many years and burned in 2002; the register and firelookout.com list it as gone. No source describes what remains.

events.note: District manned the lookout in high-risk weather; Brooks Scanlon agreed to furnish a secondary lookout facility (1967 annual report)
Abandoned cabin burned; the register and firelookout.com say a vandal, while another account says a drunken person with a disabled vehicle
Added to the Forest Fire Lookout Association register on January 7, 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register names Cascade Timberlands LLC as the administrator. The register's description says Brooks-Scanlon built the cabin, and the 1967 entry lists Brooks Scanlon with the Oregon Department of Forestry. These describe different periods; no source says when the administrator changed.

notes_for_editor: Three sources, all short. The 1940s build date is a decade-wide range with no exact year, so no built event is recorded. The 2002 burning has two accounts: the register and firelookout.com say a vandal, the Oregon lookouts page describes a drunken person in a disabled vehicle who was charged; that is unresolved. Access and visitor status are unknown in every source read; the record's access 'unknown' is kept, and no access fact was written. Owner history is unclear: the register says Cascade Timberlands LLC, the 1967 report implies Brooks Scanlon with state forestry. A 1991 Forest Service eligibility study of Deschutes National Forest fire lookouts (State Library of Oregon, digitalcollections.library.oregon.gov/nodes/view/275303) may cover this site; the PDF was not read, so it is a lead, not a source.
